habitat: Wikipedia says it breeds in Europe and Asia and migrates to Africa for the northern winter. Newman has no species page, so no Kruger habitat is stored from that account.
summary: Newman has no species page. The description is from Wikipedia. A medium-sized crake with buff- or grey-streaked brownish-black upper parts, chestnut markings on the wings, and blue-grey underparts with rufous and white bars on the flanks and undertail. The bill is flesh-toned, the iris pale brown, and the legs pale grey. Juveniles are similar to adults. The male’s call is a loud krek krek. It is larger than African Crake, which is darker and has a plainer face. Months are unset. The Kemp name Corncrake and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: African Crake is smaller and darker, with a plainer face, a red eye and a pinkish bill. Corn Crake has blue-grey underparts and chestnut wing markings.

research.note: Newman has no species page, so the plumage and the call are from the cited Wikipedia article. Length is from Wikipedia (27–30 cm). Wikipedia says it migrates to Africa for the northern winter, so status is palearctic-migrant. Kruger months are not given, so monthsPresent is unset. Avibase does not mark it rare. The grade A call is from Finland. Population figures and the Kemp name Corncrake were left unchanged.
